references.text: Simon Peter's reaction after the miraculous catch shows that his obedience to Jesus' words in verse 5 led to a revelation of Jesus' divine power.
A parallel event after the resurrection where the disciples fished all night without catching anything, but at Jesus' word they cast the net and made an enormous catch.
Mary says to the servants: 'Do whatever he tells you.' The same principle of obedience to Jesus' words, as Simon obeyed Jesus' command despite his own experience.
'Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain.' Simon had struggled all night without result, but when he acted on the Lord's word, the work was blessed.
God's word does not return empty, but accomplishes what He desires. Simon's obedience to Jesus' words ('at your word') shows the power of the word to accomplish what seems impossible.
The disciples obey Jesus' words in a situation that appears hopeless, and Jesus demonstrates His power over nature—a recurring theme in the Gospel of Luke.
'So faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.' Simon acted in faith on Jesus' words, despite human experience speaking against it.
'Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.' Simon set aside his own fishing experience and trusted in Jesus' words.
Abraham left in obedience to God's call without knowing where he was going. Similarly, Simon obeyed Jesus' words even though it contradicted all his professional knowledge and experience.
Jesus asks: 'Why do you call me "Lord, Lord," and not do what I say?' Simon calls Jesus 'Master' (Epistates) and then acts in obedience to His words.
